category.stage_note: The category has heard 'agent memory' and 'spec-driven' many times and the language has gone flat and abstract. Mem0, Zep, Letta and Supermemory all claim to remember; Kiro and Spec Kit all claim specs as source of truth. A bigger claim about remembering more will not land. Schwartz's jaded stage calls for a NEW MECHANISM, and PCM has one: the memory is your Git repository, the files are plain text, and a validator checks them. Lead with the mechanism.

style.register: Category copy is abstract and feature-forward. 'Dedicated memory layer', 'temporal knowledge graph', 'stateful agents'. Almost none of it names the reader's actual Tuesday.
notes: Top results are listicles ranking tools by capability grid, so buyers arrive already comparing feature tables.
The strongest lines in the space name a felt moment: 'no more re-explaining' beats 'dedicated memory layer'.
Nothing in the top results mentions whether the stored state is TRUE or just stored. That gap is open ground.

cultural.moment: Widespread developer fatigue with AI-generated project state that nobody can verify
cultural.relevance: Spec-driven threads now argue about drift and whether the shared spec stays true. The conversation has moved from 'can agents remember' to 'can we trust what they remembered'.

cultural.moment: Context windows framed as RAM rather than storage
cultural.relevance: The mental model the audience already holds. 'Context is RAM, memory is storage' lets a story argue that the project's state belongs in storage the project owns.

cultural.moment: Verification and reproducibility anxiety across AI-assisted research and engineering
cultural.relevance: Claims about prior agent runs are becoming a liability. A story that promises inspectable evidence rides the mood.
